description: Does this offer match the terms you supplied? Before an agent accepts an offer, contract_price_match compares the offer's unit price with the applicable term among the terms you supply, and signs the result when signing succeeds. No model is involved: the result is arithmetic and exact comparison, and anyone holding the same input can recompute it. You supply the terms; Tanilo does not hold or look up your contracts. Three results: verified, contradicted, or indeterminate with a reason. A verified result says the price matches the supplied term. Whether to pay is your policy's decision. A valid signature shows which key signed these bytes and that they have not changed since. It does not show that the supplied terms were genuine. POST /v1/verify-facts is live in free beta, rate-limited, no key needed.

agent_id.description: Optional agent identifier recorded in the receipt; otherwise the receipt carries the placeholder urn:tanilo:verify-facts:anonymous

claim_hash.description: Optional subject.claim_hash. Any hash that identifies the purchase for you; by default the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the input object is used.

offered_at.description: When the offer was made, RFC 3339 UTC, e.g. "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z"

quantity.description: Quantity offered, as a decimal string, e.g. "1"

unit.description: Unit the price applies to, e.g. "call"

unit_price.description: Offered price per unit, as a decimal string, e.g. "2.00"

terms.description: The terms you supply (caller-supplied, not verified as genuine). May be empty: the result is then indeterminate with reason no_applicable_term.

price_per_unit.description: Flat price per unit; omit when tiers are given

tiers.description: Quantity tiers; each runs from min_quantity up to, but not including, max_quantity

name: check-contract-price
